scenes.heading: Symbol and operation puzzles
scenes.say: Triangle plus triangle equals fourteen. What is the triangle? In symbol puzzles, shapes hide numbers and new signs get new rules. Let us crack them step by step.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A secret code: once you crack one letter, the rest get easier
scenes.science: Solve the clue with one shape first, then swap it into the others
scenes.breaks: a code letter can mean anything. Here every clue must still be true maths when you swap in the numbers.
scenes.say: Think of a secret code. Once you crack one letter, you can swap it in everywhere and the rest gets easier. Symbol puzzles work the same way: solve the clue with just one shape first, then substitute. Unlike a code, every clue must still be true maths.

scenes.heading: One shape first
scenes.question: ● + ● + ● = 18 and ● + ★ = 10. Find ★.
scenes.say: Three circles make eighteen, so one circle is six. Swap it in: six plus star is ten, so star is four. Careful: six is the circle, not the star.
scenes.caption: ● + ● + ● = 18, so ● = 6. Then 6 + ★ = 10, so ★ = 4.

scenes.heading: Made-up operations
scenes.say: A made-up sign comes with its own rule. Here, a diamond b means a times b, minus a. The first number fills a, the second fills b. So four diamond five is twenty minus four, which is sixteen, not fifteen.
scenes.caption: a ◇ b = a × b − a. First number → a, second → b. 4 ◇ 5 = 20 − 4 = 16.

scenes.heading: Missing signs: × and ÷ first
scenes.say: When you choose missing signs, remember the order of operations: times and divide before plus and minus. Eight times two plus three is nineteen. But eight plus two times three is fourteen, not thirty.

scenes.heading: Sum and difference
scenes.question: ★ + ▲ = 17 and ★ − ▲ = 5. Find ▲.
scenes.say: Star plus triangle is seventeen and star minus triangle is five. Add them and halve for the big one: twenty-two halved is eleven. Then triangle is seventeen take eleven, which is six.
scenes.caption: ★ = (17 + 5) ÷ 2 = 11, so ▲ = 17 − 11 = 6.

scenes.heading: Common traps
scenes.say: Watch out for these traps. Giving the value of the wrong symbol, so underline what is asked. Swapping a and b. And reading square times square as double the square. It means the number times itself.

Quick recap. Solve the clue with one shape first, then substitute. In made-up operations, the first number fills a. Do times and divide before plus and minus. And re-read what the question asks. Now try the practice questions!
